results.content: * 1 in 3 BFSI employees plan to quit: 3 workforce imperatives that will decide the next decade. ## Great Place To Work India warns of a BFSI retention and skills crisis, urges stronger leadership, AI aligned with roles, and faster learning, names Indias Best Workplaces in BFSI 2026. Great Place To Work India report reveals BFSI retention risks, AI adoption gaps, and highlights Indias Best Workplaces in BFSI 2026 driving future ready talent. India’s Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance sector is facing a looming retention crisis, with one in three employees currently planning to leave their jobs. The BFSI sector operates at the intersection of scale, scrutiny, and speed, which is driving three core challenges: building financial resilience amid volatility, meeting intensified regulatory and compliance demands, and accelerating AI and digital adoption on legacy systems. I congratulate the winners of India’s Best Workplaces in BFSI 2026 for fostering a future-ready culture that enables people to adapt and thrive at scale." Balbir Singh, CEO, Great Place To Work India.

EBAday 2026 will host internationally recognised fintech futurist and bestselling author Brett King as the challenge speaker, highlighting how Agentic AI will make the industry completely rethink money and payments. Image 6: Brett King announced as challenge speaker at EBAday 2026 in Copenhagen. Taking place from 16–17 June in Copenhagen, Denmark, EBAday will challenge banks, payment providers, and infrastructure leaders to confront how AI-led transformation is now accelerating and already reshaping competitive advantage across financial services. Brett King’s presentation will start with the rise of agentic AI today and explore how autonomous AI agents are now capable of reasoning, executing tasks, and transacting on behalf of individuals and businesses. This evolution marks a shift from AI as a productivity tool to AI as an economic actor, with direct implications for how payments, commerce, and financial decisions are made. ### Download Finextra News.

results.title: India manufacturing PMI rises to 54.7 in April, growth remains subdued - Business Standard
results.content: Home / Markets / Capital Market News / India manufacturing PMI rises to 54.7 in April, growth remains subdued. # India manufacturing PMI rises to 54.7 in April, growth remains subdued. Last Updated : May 04 2026 | 2:16 PMIST. Indias manufacturing sector saw a slight improvement in April, with the HSBC India Manufacturing PMI rising from 53.9 in March to 54.7. Gains in new orders and production were modest and remained among the weakest since 2022, although exports stood out as a strong area, growing at their fastest pace since last September. While firms continued to purchase inputs, growth in buying activity slowed to one of the weakest levels in two-and-a-half years. ## Godrej Properties consolidated net profit rises 70.13% in the March 2026 quarter. ## Nalin Lease Finance standalone net profit rises 29.82% in the March 2026 quarter. ## Key Corp reports standalone net loss of Rs 9.62 crore in the March 2026 quarter.
